source_candidates.title: Building trust in AI agents: A production-ready evaluation framework with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
verified_facts: AWS describes nine evaluation stages and three evaluation levels for a multi-agent sales analytics system.
The team reports fluent numerical errors that uptime monitoring did not detect, including wrong units, swapped metrics and unsupported calculations.
The article uses a 15-case sentinel, 200-case pre-production gate and 30-minute canary windows, while identifying some example values as illustrative.

source_candidates.title: Introducing Reflection Beam: an open-weight model for agentic coding on AWS
verified_facts: AWS documents a 501-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23 billion active parameters and Apache 2.0 weights.
The guide covers managed JumpStart deployment and Kubernetes-based HyperPod paths using JumpStart, SGLang or vLLM.
It recommends pinned artifacts, configuration validation, smoke tests and measurement of time to first token, token latency, end-to-end latency and throughput.

source_candidates.title: Fast-Growth Companies Have the Biggest AI Opportunity, Few Are Capturing It
verified_facts: SAP reports survey research conducted with Oxford Economics and states AI is used in roughly one quarter of business tasks.
The article says nine percent of surveyed organizations have fundamentally adapted their businesses around AI.
SAP argues that process, data, governance and business readiness constrain scaling, but the article is vendor-sponsored and no independent replication was reviewed.
source_candidates.freshness_reason: Extended fallback is justified because this is the freshest verified primary research in the selection that quantifies the gap between task-level AI use and process-level operating change, and it remains within 168 hours.

source_candidates.title: 10 Questions Board Members Should Be Asking About Security and Compliance
verified_facts: SAP presents ten board-level questions spanning accountability, decision rights, risk visibility, regulatory change, suppliers and incident recovery.
The article recommends continuous security and compliance evidence instead of annual point-in-time review.
It asks boards to connect combined incident and business-continuity exercises with owners and unresolved remediation actions.

source_candidates.title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more autonomy without losing control
verified_facts: AWS organizes agent controls into five layers: scope, know, bound, observe and prove.
The framework places enforceable policies outside an agent's reasoning and gives each agent its own identity and least privilege.
It distinguishes precisely provable rules from contextual decisions that still need human judgment.

source_candidates.title: Agent Skills
verified_facts: Microsoft defines Skills as portable folders containing SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references and assets.
The documented expense-report example separates policy guidance, a deterministic validation script and a reusable report template.
Microsoft warns that scripts execute source-supplied code, recommends approvals and distinguishes focused low-risk Skills from checkpointed workflows with side effects.
